title: Keystone-18TH Tapped Bass Horn — λ/2 Dual-Side Loading vs Front-Loaded Horn
description: Simulates a Danley/Keystone-inspired tapped bass horn where the rear of the 18" cone feeds an expanding 2.17 m closed-throat wave-inverting line while the front cone radiates directly into the mouth tap — delivering extraordinary 30–60 Hz output per liter with dual cone-excursion nulls.
design_notes: Dual-Side Phase-Inversion Physics: Below 85 Hz, the 2.17 m throat-to-tap path delays the inverted rear wave by λ/4..λ/2 so both sides of the diaphragm sum constructively (+6 dB) at the mouth while air mass clamps cone excursion at 33 Hz and 72 Hz!

Tapped vs Front-Loaded Trade-Off: Compare Variant 3 (1× Keystone-18TH) against Variant 4 (1× TerraHorn-18 Front-Loaded Horn). The tapped horn wins by +3.5 dB from 30–50 Hz in a 10% smaller box and runs cooler (open magnet in high-velocity tap airflow!), but exhibits a sharp λ cancellation notch above 115 Hz — demanding a strict ≤ 92 Hz LR24 crossover.
Inspect the 3D CAD Cutaway & Side Blueprint: Notice the internal Tap-Junction Driver Baffle near the front mouth with both rear-throat (pink) and front-tap (cyan) paths traced in millimeters.
